proposedScope: Prewar exterior of the Republican Palace Museum in the former All Saints Cathedral, including the west narthex, nave, transepts, chancel and the campanile if its completed layout can be confirmed.

auxiliaryFootprints.finding: No separate footprint aligns with the planned tower position. Use the plan as an approximate placement control, with the later consecration as evidence that the tower was built.

excluded.reason: Native Commons record dedicates the photographed stained glass as old public-domain artwork and licenses the 2007 photograph under CC BY-SA 3.0. The image lacks exterior coverage.
The anonymous external photograph has a Sudan expiration tag. Its first-publication history remains uncertain.

originalPublication.publicationEvidence: The 24 November 1915 issue prints the Royal Academy drawing and its contemporary article. The architect died in 1951. The two scans reproduce the single published plate and its ground plan.
originalPublication.useLimit: The November 1915 article still describes an unbuilt campanile. The eventual appearance and location require later evidence before modeling it as built.

planControls.mainShape: Cruciform plan with gabled nave, west narthex, transepts and a straight east termination.
planControls.westElevation: Stone rubble and dressed corners, a pointed central portal, six circular grilles around a central circular grille and paired upper lights.
planControls.campanile: Detached at the southwest corner, linked to the narthex by a roofed passage. The published proposal shows a clock stage, an open lantern and a small pyramidal cap.
planControls.limitations: Plan dimensions are estimates read from the printed graphic scale. The completed tower may differ in exact dimensions.

laterConditionSources.fact: Reports the museum ransacked during the conflict.
Reports a post-conflict assessment of the wider Republican Palace complex. Present exterior condition of the former cathedral remains uncertain.
The bishop’s papers catalogue records Sudan Daily Herald reports on the completed tower and baptistery consecration.
The architectural study identifies the completed tower as the Lee Stack memorial and cites an illustrated report from 7 February 1931.

scope: The prewar Republican Palace Museum in the former All Saints Cathedral, Khartoum. Include the cruciform masonry church, raised west entry, campanile and covered passage to the narthex.
geometryBasis: The 12-point OpenStreetMap outline fixes the approximately 57 m by 25 m cruciform shell. Schultz’s 1915 plan places the separate campanile to the southwest and shows the covered passage linking it to the church.
sectionBasis: The 1912 account specifies yellow and pale-red sandstone, green glazed roof tile, deep eaves, two feet from ground to terrace and four feet from terrace to the church floor. The west drawing shows the pointed portal, clustered rose lights, hoods, and the separate clock and belfry stages.

firstPublishedMaterials.basis: Written contemporary description of sandstone colors, green glazed corrugated tiles, raised terrace, floor and ventilation hoods.
